result.detail: Cloudflare has self-managed OAuth clients. Apps start `private`, so only members of the creating account can use them. To let any Cloudflare user authorize, the developer sets `public` visibility. That needs the developer to verify the client domain, which is a domain-ownership step. The docs I read describe no Cloudflare review, approval or listing step. They state no cap on installs, users or clients. Per-customer API tokens also work with no gate. Caveat: the docs don't say whether Cloudflare runs the domain verification or the developer does it automatically, so this is the closest thing to a gate. The docs say domain verification only confirms the owner controls the domain. Account admins can also block new public OAuth app authorizations for their own account.
result.quote: To make an application available to any Cloudflare user, complete the prerequisites for `public` visibility.
